description.value: The study tested whether increased frequency of social interaction acts as a social reward and whether reward-system activation is modulated by individual interaction preferences.

spans.text: Therefore, we hypothesized that social interaction itself activates the reward system in a manner that depends upon individual interaction preferences.

design.value: A functional magnetic resonance imaging study in which participants played a virtual ball-toss game with normal- and high-frequency social interaction conditions, together with a button-press control run.

spans.text: To test this hypothesis, we conducted a functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) study in which 38 participants played a virtual ball-toss game in which the number of ball tosses to the participant was either similar to (normal-frequency condition) or higher than (high-frequency condition) the number of tosses to the other players.
Participants completed the Collectivism Scale22, a 14-item scale that measures allocentric tendency.

task_description.value: Participants played a virtual ball-toss game with four same-gender players unknown to them.

spans.text: In the ball-toss run, the participants were required to play a virtual ball-toss game19,20,58,59 with four same-gender players that were unknown to them.
There was one run of the ball-toss task, consisting of six ball-toss blocks, six rating blocks, and six rest blocks.
